summary: Mainstream Indian cricket storylines and globally recognized icons like Cristiano Ronaldo and Yash drive over 80% of total viewership. Niche international athletes, financial stock updates, commodity rates, and civic rankings consistently stall below 100 views. To drive explosive growth toward monetisation, restrict coverage to tier-one cricket and marquee viral moments while perfecting seamless loops. Ensure Roman Hinglish titles feature prominent star names and specific stats right up front.
do_more: Focus on mainstream Indian cricket superstars (Arshdeep Singh, Hardik Pandya, Rohit Sharma) and high-stakes IPL news
Feature household global sports figures like Cristiano Ronaldo who have massive mainstream followings in India
Include high-impact numbers and unique milestones directly in the story (e.g., No. 11, 13 times sold)
Script tight 40-second narratives that seamlessly loop the ending back into the opening hook line
avoid: Covering niche international athletes like Brajan Gruda or obscure tennis updates with low Indian interest
Producing finance, stock market, gold price, or municipal city cleanliness explainers
Writing vague, nameless titles like 'Debutant ka Dhamaka' that fail to state who or what is featured
Wasting the first three seconds on greetings, logos, or slow contextual build-up
hook_tips: Open with an unexpected stat: 'No. 11 par aakar kisi Indian pacer ne aisa chhakka pehle kabhi nahi mara!'
Pique curiosity around star decisions: 'Ronaldo apni iconic Jersey No. 7 kyu chhod rahe hain?'
Highlight immediate drama: 'Match se theek pehle Team India do alag hisso mein kyu bat gayi?'
Deliver the core tension in under 2 seconds without introductory fluff
title_tips: Place the star or team name in the first three words (e.g., 'Arshdeep Singh Record: No 11 Par Six!')
Use exact numbers or milestones to spark instant interest (e.g., '13 Baar Bike! IPL Ka Sabse Anokha Record')
Use punchy punctuation (! or ?) to highlight genuine drama without resorting to fake clickbait
